question:
Fill in the following blanks:

(i) The reciprocal of 0 is ....

(ii) The numbers .... and .... are their own reciprocals.

(iii) If $y$ be the reciprocal of $x$, then the reciprocal of $y^{2}$ in terms of $x$ will be .....

(iv) The product of a non-zero rational number and its reciprocal is  $ \cdots\cdots\cdots $.

(v) The reciprocal of a negative rational number is  $ \cdots\cdots $.

glassboxSteps.why: No number multiplied by 0 gives 1, so division by zero is undefined.
$\dfrac{1}{1}=1$ and $\dfrac{1}{-1}=-1$ — each equals its own reciprocal.
If $y=\dfrac{1}{x}$, then $y^2=\dfrac{1}{x^2}$, so its reciprocal is $x^2$.
The reciprocal of a negative number is negative ($\dfrac{1}{-a}=-\dfrac{1}{a}$).

explanation: (i) not defined · (ii) 1 and −1 · (iii) $x^2$ · (iv) 1 · (v) negative
